source_refs.note: Exercise 12.3, Question 8: continuity of a piecewise cost function at x = 10 (book p.236). Answer key PDF 310: yes.

blocks.prompt: 8 The cost to produce \(x\) units is: \[C(x) = \begin{cases} 5x + 20, & x \le 10 \\ 6x + 10, & x > 10 \end{cases}\]Is the cost function continuous at \(x = 10\)?
blocks.explanation:
A continuity question for a two-piece cost function (same type as Question 6).
We must check whether both formulas give the same cost at \(x = 10\).
Plan: find \(C(10)\), the LHL and the RHL, then test the three conditions.
steps:
Given: \(C(x) = 5x + 20\) for \(x \le 10\), \(6x + 10\) for \(x > 10\).
To find: whether \(C\) is continuous at \(x = 10\).
Method: \(C\) is continuous at \(x = c\) when (i) \(C(c)\) is defined, (ii) \(\lim_{x \to c} C(x)\) exists (LHL = RHL), (iii) \(\lim_{x \to c} C(x) = C(c)\).

Condition (i): find \(C(10)\)
\[C(10) = 5(10) + 20 = 70\]
Why: \(x \le 10\) includes 10, so the first formula is used.

Left hand limit
\[\lim_{x \to 10^-} C(x) = \lim_{x \to 10^-} (5x + 20)\]
\[= 50 + 20 = 70\]
Why: Below 10 units the first formula applies.

Right hand limit
\[\lim_{x \to 10^+} C(x) = \lim_{x \to 10^+} (6x + 10)\]
\[= 60 + 10 = 70\]
Why: Above 10 units the second formula applies.

Conditions (ii) and (iii)
\[\text{LHL} = \text{RHL} = 70 = C(10)\]
Why: All three conditions hold, so \(C\) is continuous at \(x = 10\).

Check
\[C(9.9) = 49.5 + 20 = 69.5\]
\[C(10.1) = 60.6 + 10 = 70.6\]
Why: Costs just below and just above 10 units are close to 70.
blocks.final_answer: Yes. \(C\) is continuous at \(x = 10\) (LHL \(=\) RHL \(= C(10) = 70\))
